Panel: STANFILL, C.J., and MEAD, CONNORS, LAWRENCE, DOUGLAS, and LIPEZ, JJ.
ASHLEY LYNNE
v.
DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES et al.
CONNORS, J. [¶1] When MaineCare pays the costs of medical treatment of an injury for which a third party is liable and the MaineCare recipient settles a tort claim with the third party, the Department of Health and Human Services may recover “the cost of benefits provided” by MaineCare, but only “to the extent of the recovery for medical expenses.” 22 M.R.S. § 14(1) (2026) . The question presented in this appeal is how to determine the extent to which a recipient has recovered for medical expenses, and, thus, the upper limit of the Department’s reimbursement, when a settlement between the recipient and the third party does not allocate damages between medical expenses and other damages. In this action between a recipient and the Department to determine the amount that the Department may recover , the Superior Court (Androscoggin County, 2 Archer, J.) entered summary judgment in favor of the recipient. We conclude that in order to allocate this settlement, the court must resolve disputed factual issues, and so we vacate and remand for further proceedings. I. STATE OF MAINE SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT STANDING ORDER REGARDING ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER JB-24-03 PILOT PROGRAM TO CONDITIONALLY AUTHORIZE LAW STUDENT EXTERNS TO PROVIDE PUBLIC DEFENSE SERVICES
Effective: September 4, 2026
On December 18, 2024, the Supreme Judicial Court adopted Administrative Order JB-24-03, Pilot Program to Conditionally Authorize Law Student Externs to Provide Public Defense Services. The order provides that it expires on September 5, 2026.
The Court has not determined whether to adopt the program permanently. There are, however, students enrolled in externships for the fall semester of 2026 who will be unable to participate in the externships if the order is allowed to expire.
Because it will take time to determine whether the program will be made permanent, but the Court does not wish to prevent the currently enrolled students from participating in their externships, it is hereby ORDERED that the effective term of the pilot program established by Administrative Order JB-24- 03 is extended through January 15, 2027.
The University of Maine School of Law and the organizations hosting student externs should not arrange for student externs for the spring semester of 2027 without first confirming that the pilot program will remain in effect for that semester.
Dated: September 4, 2026 For the Court:
/s/ Valerie Stanfill Chief Justice

SJC invites comments on proposed amendments to the Maine Rules of Evidence to permit parties to authenticate certain electronic evidence other than through the testimony of a foundation witness. Comments due by September 29, 2026.

Date: 9/8/2026

The Maine Supreme Judicial Court invites comments on proposed amendments to Rule 902 of the Maine Rules of Evidence that would permit a party to authenticate certain electronic evidence other than through the testimony of a foundation witness.

The proposed amendments are available at the links below.

Any comments must be filed with the Executive Clerk of the Supreme Judicial Court by 4:00 p.m. on Tuesday, September 29, 2026. Comments must be in an email sent to lawcourt.clerk@courts.maine.gov. If the comments are in an attachment to the email, the attachment must be a document in native (text-based and not scanned) portable document format (.pdf). The Clerk's Office will acknowledge receipt of the email via reply email.

All comments must contain (1) the name and mailing address of the individual submitting the comments and (2) the name, mailing address, and primary telephone number of the organization (if any) on whose behalf the comments are submitted. An individual need not be an attorney to submit comments individually or on behalf of an organization.

Comments are public documents and may be posted on the Courts website.

Judicial Branch to Hold 'Constitution Day' Student Town Hall on September 17th at the Capital Judicial Center in Augusta

Date: 9/10/2026

Supreme Judicial Court Chief Justice Valerie Stanfill and members of the Supreme Judicial Court will conduct a student-teacher town hall on Thursday, September 17, 2026, to commemorate the 239th anniversary of the signing of the U.S. Constitution.

"The Constitution is the bedrock and framework of American democracy," said Chief Justice Stanfill. "It shapes the everyday lives of young Americans, including their individual rights and freedoms, now, and in the future. We hope the student town hall will spark conversation and curiosity about the role and importance of the Constitution in establishing the U.S. as a nation based on the rule of law."

Classes and students are invited to attend and participate by Zoom or in person at the Capital Judicial Center in Augusta. Classes wishing to attend in person should RSVP to Julia.Finn@courts.maine.gov by Wednesday, September 16 at 5:00 p.m.

Constitution Day Town Hall at the Capital Judicial Center

When: Thursday, Sept. 17, 2026

Time: 10:00 a.m. - 10:55 a.m. (In person and live via a Zoom webinar. Event will be recorded and posted on the Judicial Branch website.)

Location: Capital Judicial Center, 1 Court Street, Augusta, Maine.

Format: Informal student-teacher Town Hall, with Constitution-related questions from students and teachers.

How to attend: In person, RSVP to Julia.Finn@courts.maine.gov by September 16th at 5:00. Educators, please contact Julia with any questions.

Reminders in Preparation for Maine eCourts and eFiling in Cumberland County Courts

Date: 9/23/2026

On Monday, September 28, 2026, the Maine Judicial Branch is expanding Maine eCourts to all case types in Judicial Region 2, comprising Cumberland County Unified Criminal Docket (UCD), Cumberland County Superior Court, Portland District Court, and Bridgton District Court.

All case types -- civil, family, juvenile and criminal cases -- will be included in the transition from paper filing to electronic filing. As of Monday, September 28, all mandatory electronic filers pursuant to the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems (MRECS) will be required to eFile documents in these courts. Self-represented litigants (parties who do not have attorneys) who file fewer than six cases in a calendar year will not be required to eFile.

Court Closures and Emergency Filing Procedures
To prepare for the implementation of Maine eCourts and eFiling on September 28, Region 2 courts are currently operating on a modified schedule and have emergency filing procedures in place. In addition, all Region 2 courts will be closed from 8 a.m. to noon the week of September 28th. Please refer to the schedule of closures and emergency procedures during these closings.

ShareFile Discontinued in Region 2 Courts
The ShareFile platform used in Region 2 courts will be disabled for all criminal, civil violation, juvenile filings, and GAL vouchers, at 2:00 p.m. on Thursday, September 24. Starting Monday, September 28, attorneys must instead use eFileMaine. Please note, attorney vouchers filed pursuant to the Standing Order regarding Payment to Court-Appointed Counsel will continue to be accepted by ShareFile for a grace period of 60 days.

Training Resources
For attorneys and staff who are new to using eFileMaine, we highly recommend viewing the recorded videos, particularly the video excerpts, available on the Maine eCourts Trainings and Resources web page. In addition to the recordings, the information and resources available on the Maine eCourts Trainings and Resources web page offer guidance for setting up your eFileMaine account and instructions to eFile documents successfully.

Personal Identifying Information (PII) Attachment (CR-CV-JV-297)
Pursuant to the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems (MRECS) filers are responsible for omitting or redacting nonpublic information in electronically filed documents. If the filer decides to omit rather than redact, the personal identifying information must be included on this form.

The PII form should be uploaded as an attachment to the associated filing document, in the same way that an exhibit is submitted.

Online Fine Payments
As of September 28th, parties who wish to make criminal fine payments online for cases in Cumberland County will be directed to the new online payment portal, Maine eCourts Criminal Fines and Fees. Visit Maine eCourts: Pay a Court Fine to learn more.

Support
Support for eFiling is available by emailing ecourtshelp@courts.maine.gov or by calling (207) 213-2813, Monday through Thursday from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.

For more information on Maine eCourts and eFiling, visit: https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/index.html

Supreme Judicial Court to Hold Oral Arguments at Three Maine High Schools

Date: 9/29/2026

The Supreme Judicial Court will hold court and hear a total of nine cases at three Maine high schools next week.

On Tuesday, October 6, beginning at 9:00 a.m., the Court will visit Katahdin Middle/High School in Stacyville to hear arguments in three appellate cases. Senator Trey Stewart extended the invitation to the Law Court. The three cases are scheduled to begin at 9:00 a.m., 10:00 a.m., and 11:00 a.m.

The Court will hear three appeals at Morse High School in Bath on Wednesday, October 7 at the invitation of Senator Denise Tepler. The Court will follow the same schedule with the first oral argument starting at 9:00 a.m., the second at 10:00 a.m., and the third at 11:00 a.m.

And on Thursday, October 8, the Court will hear three cases at Kennebunk High School at the invitation of Representative Daniel Sayre. Again, the schedule indicates that the first case starts at 9:00 a.m.

Students receive copies of the briefs in advance and, after each argument, the lawyers stay to answer questions from interested students. When the cases are decided, the schools receive a link to the decisions to share with the students.

Beginning in 2005, the Court has held oral arguments in actual appellate cases at over 40 Maine high schools around the state. In each school, the gymnasium, cafeteria, or auditorium is turned into a courtroom for the morning so that the students can observe the appellate process. The Court has visited schools from York County to Aroostook County; from Oxford County to Washington County; and many places in between.

Chief Justice Valerie Stanfill said, "We hope that providing real-time exposure to the third branch of government supplements the students' civics education and exposes Maine learners to the concept of justice. The practice of appellate law is rarely seen on television or in the movies. Creating a courtroom environment in a high school takes great effort on the part of the school administration and staff and we appreciate their extensive efforts."

The press is welcome to attend. The case schedule has been posted on the Courts website here.

Live video streaming of these cases, and all other Supreme Judicial Court oral arguments, is available here.

If interviews or photographs are desired while the Court is at the schools, please contact Julie Finn beforehand to schedule an interview at the below email address. Photographs and video of students are subject to the rules of the high school, and the press is requested to contact school officials directly.

Maine eCourts Scheduled to be Implemented in Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc, and Waldo Courts in December

Date: 10/9/2026

The Maine Judicial Branch announced today that District and Superior Courts in Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc, and Waldo counties (comprising Judicial Region 6) will transition from paper filing to electronic filing (eFiling) on Monday, December 7, 2026. All case types in the Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County Unified Criminal Dockets (UCDs) and Superior Courts; and in the Belfast, Rockland, West Bath, and Wiscasset District Courts will transition to eFiling. To help attorneys and other stakeholders in Region 6 get ready for eFiling, the Judicial Branch will hold a virtual presentation by Zoom:

Topic: Maine eCourts in Region 6: Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County
Date & Time: Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 12:00 p.m.
Please click the link below to join the webinar:
https://courts-maine-gov.zoom.us/j/96415858276
Passcode: 522889

The Zoom presentation will be recorded and posted on the Maine eCourts Training & Resources page following the live session.

eFiler Trainings for Attorneys and Staff
Members of the Maine eCourts project team will conduct in-person training for attorneys and staff according to the schedule below. Please note, registration is required to attend a training session. Prosecutors and staff will receive a separate link to register by email.

  • Prosecutor eFiler Training - Thursday, November 5th from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. (Knox County Superior Court, Rockland) Registration link to be sent by email
  • All Other eFiler Training Monday, November 2nd from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. (Knox County Superior Court, Rockland) Register for this session

Region 6 Will Be the Second to Last Judicial Region to Complete the Transition to eFiling
When Region 6 courts transition to eFiling on December 7, they will be the second-to-last judicial region to implement eFiling. Earlier this year, courts in Judicial Regions 2, 7, 8, 1, and 4 made the switch from paper filing to eFiling. The Maine Judicial Branch remains on track to have all courts on the new system by February 2027.

Supreme Judicial Court Chief Justice Valerie Stanfill noted, "We are pleased that the transition from paper filing to eFiling has proceeded so smoothly this year, a testament to the hard work and dedication of all Judicial Branch staff. The eCourts project implementation and project support teams have traveled all over the state to make the transition successful, and they certainly deserve special acknowledgement."

Who Is Required to eFile?
Attorneys, government agencies (except law enforcement agencies), and parties who file more than six non-emergency cases in a calendar year, are required to eFile in courts that have implemented Maine eCourts. Self-represented parties are not required to eFile and can continue to file documents as they always have, in paper at the courthouse, by mail, or by email if filing a protection from abuse or harassment case.

About Maine eCourts
Maine eCourts is a suite of applications and web-based tools provided by Tyler Technologies' Enterprise Justice Software. The system allows for the management of court dockets and hearings, storage of digital case files, eFiling, and online payments.

For more information about Maine eCourts visit: https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/index.html

To receive updates from the Maine Judicial Branch on Maine eCourts and other news, sign up for our mailing list at: https://www.courts.maine.gov/news/signup.html

Reminder: Maine eCourts in Region 6 (Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County) Virtual Presentation Today at Noon

Date: 10/14/2026

To help attorneys and other stakeholders in Region 6 get ready for eFiling, the Judicial Branch will hold a virtual presentation by Zoom today.

Topic: Maine eCourts in Region 6: Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County
Date & Time: Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 12:00 p.m.
Please click the link below to join the webinar:
https://courts-maine-gov.zoom.us/j/96415858276
Passcode: 522889

The Zoom presentation will be recorded and posted on the Maine eCourts Training & Resources page following the live session.

District and Superior Courts in Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc, and Waldo counties (comprising Judicial Region 6) will transition from paper filing to electronic filing (eFiling) on Monday, December 7, 2026. This includes all case types in the Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County Unified Criminal Dockets (UCDs) and Superior Courts; and in the Belfast, Rockland, West Bath, and Wiscasset District Courts.

Who Is Required to eFile?
Attorneys, government agencies (except law enforcement agencies), and parties who file more than six non-emergency cases in a calendar year, are required to eFile in courts that have implemented Maine eCourts. Self-represented parties are not required to eFile and can continue to file documents as they always have, in paper at the courthouse, by mail, or by email if filing a protection from abuse or harassment case.

About Maine eCourts
Maine eCourts is a suite of applications and web-based tools provided by Tyler Technologies' Enterprise Justice Software. The system allows for the management of court dockets and hearings, storage of digital case files, eFiling, and online payments.

For more information about Maine eCourts visit: https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/index.html

To receive updates from the Maine Judicial Branch on Maine eCourts and other news, sign up for our mailing list at: https://www.courts.maine.gov/news/signup.html

STANDING ORDER REQUIRING PAPER FILING FOR ELECTION DAY 2026 EMERGENCY MATTERS
The Maine Judicial Branch (MJB) is implementing the Maine eCourts system – including eFiling – statewide.1 EFileMaine is a practical and efficient document submission system already in use in many courts throughout the state. However, because filings related to Election Day may be uniquely time- sensitive, to ensure timely processing, the MJB will require paper filing under the limited circumstances described below.

It is further ORDERED that the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems are SUSPENDED to the extent necessary to give effect to this order.

Judicial Branch Announces Procedure for Emergency Case Filings Regarding Elections

Date: 10/29/2026

AUGUSTA, Maine. The Maine Judicial Branch announced the procedure for emergency case filings regarding elections to be held on November 3, 2026.

Procedure for Election Filings

In order to expedite the review of filings, Superior Court Chief Justice Robert Mullen and District Court Chief Judge Brent Davis issued a standing order on October 28th requiring all filings pertaining to the November 3 election and filed between Friday, October 30, 2026, at 4:00 pm and Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 9:00 pm to be filed on paper at the clerk's office. Filers should NOT use the eFile Maine system for these emergency filings.

Filings submitted on paper will be reviewed immediately by a clerk and can be directed to the appropriate justice for timely review. Filers are also encouraged to put their cell phone numbers or emergency telephone numbers (where they can be reached after hours) on their filings.

State Courts Open Late on November 3

The state courthouses in Bangor, Augusta and Portland will be open until 9:00 p.m. for the purpose of accepting and acting on emergency paper filings regarding elections. A judge, a clerk and a marshal will be on duty at each courthouse.

Availability of Documents to the Media

All public documents related to election filings will be posted on the high-profile page of the Judicial Branchs public website as soon as is practicable.

Judicial Branch Issues Amendment to Administrative Order on the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems (MRECS), Effective November 2, 2026

Date: 11/2/2026

The Maine Judicial Branch announced today that an Administrative Order on rules and procedures applicable to Maine eCourts and eFiling has been amended regarding the use of non-Judicial Branch court forms when one has been provided by the court.

AO JB 20-03 (A. 11-26) was adopted in 2020 to provide guidance on the applicability of the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems (MRECS) during the transitional period during the implementation of Maine eCourts and electronic filing when there are conflicts between MRECS and other Judicial Branch rules and administrative orders.

New Section I.C. of JB 20-20 provides that "[i]f an applicable court-approved form exists and is available to the public, the parties must use it" and further adds the following requirement:

"If a filer does not use a form, the filer must include a brief explanation in a cover letter accompanying the submission that indicates the existing form is not suitable."

Barbara Cardone, Director of Legal Affairs and Public Relations explained the reason for the amendment. "The reason for the amendment is to increase the efficiency of reviewing eFiling submissions. eFilers who submit non-Judicial Branch-approved court forms can avoid having their submission rejected by including an explanatory cover letter with the eFiling. We hope this clarification helps the eFiling and legal community's smooth transition to eFiling and Maine eCourts."

AO JB 20-03 (A. 11-26) has been posted on the Administrative Orders page of the Judicial Branch website at https://www.courts.maine.gov/adminorders/index.html

Judicial Branch Ends Attorney Entry Screening Bypass Program and Announces Procedure for Reimbursement

Date: 11/17/2026

Beginning January 1, 2027, attorneys entering state courthouses will no longer be able to bypass security screening. Attorneys who show their bar cards (which can be downloaded from the Board of Bar Overseers website) will be able to go to the head of the screening line. In some courthouses, there may be a separate "attorneys only" line if resources allow.

Chief Justice Stanfill spoke to the policy change: The Judicial Branch continuously reviews our security protocols to ensure appropriate measures are in place. We believe this policy change provides greater protection for all people using the courthouse. The policy change follows best practices for courthouse security and aligns with the policy of the federal courts in Maine and the state courts of most other New England states.

The Judicial Branch stopped issuing security cards to attorneys in May 2026. Attorneys whose security cards have not expired by January 1, 2027, will be able to receive a pro rata refund of the fee for the unexpired portion. Instructions and the form for requesting a refund are posted on the For Attorneys page of the Judicial Branch website and can be downloaded directly here: https://www.courts.maine.gov/attorneys/atty-security-card-reimbursement.pdf
